Hi Daniela. Before Thursday, can you give me the Brazil numbers for the third quarter? Let us start with online sales.
Sure. Online sales increased by eighteen percent. Our target was fifteen, so we were above target.
Excellent. And the checkout? That is the number the directors really want to see.
There was a sharp drop in the average checkout time. It dropped from ninety seconds to forty-five.
From ninety to forty-five? So customers wait half the time now. What about support tickets?
They dropped by thirty percent, to seven hundred a month. The new system has fewer problems.
Great. And the mobile app? The directors love that percentage.
App users increased every month, a steady increase. But we had two hundred and fifty thousand users, and the target was three hundred thousand.
There was a sharp drop in the checkout time.

The number of app users increased steadily.

Hi Daniela, it is Sarah, your English coach. On Thursday you are going to present your quarterly results, so here are three tips for talking about numbers. First, the small words are very important. Use by for the difference: sales increased by eighteen percent. Use from and to for the start and the end: the checkout time dropped from ninety seconds to forty-five. Second, be careful with fifteen and fifty. In fifteen, the stress is at the end: fif-teen. In fifty, the stress is at the start: fif-ty. And we say eighteen percent, never eighteen percents. Third, do not read every number on the slide. The directors want a story, not a list. Choose the three most important numbers, say if the change was sharp or steady, and always compare it with your target. Were you higher or lower than the target? That is the first thing they want to know. Good luck on Thursday, Daniela.

Hi Daniela, it is Greg. I have the numbers from the US stores for the third quarter, and they are not great. Online sales increased slightly, by only four percent. Our target was ten percent, so we are below target. The average checkout time did not change much. It is still about eighty seconds. And in August, support tickets increased sharply, by forty percent, because of the bug in the payment page. In September they dropped again, after the patch. Your numbers in Brazil are much better than ours, especially the checkout time. On Thursday, the directors are going to ask you one question: how did your team do it? So please prepare two or three minutes about the new checkout system. Thanks, Daniela. See you on Thursday.

First, online sales increased by eighteen percent, and we were above our target. Then, there was a sharp drop in the average checkout time, from ninety seconds to forty-five. After that, support tickets dropped by thirty percent, to seven hundred a month. Next, app users increased steadily, but they were lower than our target. Finally, our goal for the fourth quarter is a steady increase in app users.
